subject: Post-call: Budget & volume validation / pricing targets (Acme Payments)
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Nguyen <lisa.nguyen@acmepay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + budget range validation (Acme Payments)

Thanks for the time this morning, Lisa - appreciate the clear context. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can size a committed pricing option for procurement: 

Key notes from our call:
- Workloads: payments fraud-detection enrichment + chat support (mostly 1k-2k token calls, some longer batch reranking).
- Expected monthly volumes: baseline ~200M tokens/month, seasonal/peak up to ~800M tokens/month (spiky Q4 and marketing promos).
- Target unit economics you mentioned: aiming for roughly $300 / 1M tokens as the target to make the economics work internally (confirming).
- Procurement thresholds you shared: PO/SOW required for anything >$50k/mo; VP approval for spends >$150k/mo. Please correct if I misremembered.

Open items for us to propose a firm commit: 
1) Confirm the baseline vs peak split you expect to commit to (e.g., 200M committed + on-demand burst to 800M, or a single commit band).
2) Confirm target $/1M tokens floor (you said ~$300) and whether that's an aspirational target or a hard procurement requirement.
3) Procurement contact + timeline (if we propose a 12-mo committed discount, who signs and timelines for PO/SOW?).

Next steps: I'll draft a 2-option pricing estimate (committed tier + on-demand overflow) and send it over today for you and procurement to review. Attaching a short product/pricing sheet for context.

Attachment: redwood-product-sheet.pdf (summary), will follow with detailed pricing estimate (PDF).

Thanks - Monica
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Lisa Nguyen <lisa.nguyen@acmepay.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ramos <tom.ramos@acmepay.com>, procurement@acmepay.com
Date: 2026-03-20T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + budget range validation (Acme Payments)

Thanks Monica - that's accurate and helpful. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) Volumes: baseline 200M/mo is our conservative estimate. We expect average 200-350M most months, but we need the ability to spike to ~800M for promo periods. Ideally we'd do a committed baseline (200M) + burst envelope.
2) Unit economics: $300 / 1M tokens is what our finance team has penciled in as the target for us to avoid re-architecting current systems - it's effectively our target ceiling for pricing on this workload. If you can get us to $300 or below with reasonable commit terms, procurement will be engaged.
3) Procurement thresholds: correct - PO/SOW required >$50k/month, VP sign-off for >$150k/month. If monthly run-rate is projected to exceed $200k we usually require a short competitive review (but not a full RFP unless >$250k/mo).

Procurement lead is Tom Ramos (cc'd) - Tom, we are evaluating Redwood for inference. Can you advise preferred procurement docs and whether a 12-mo commit at the proposed rates will be acceptable subject to PO?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

- Lisa
Lisa Nguyen
Head of ML Platform
Acme Payments
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-20T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + budget range validation (Acme Payments)

Nice - confirming I captured the ask: baseline 200M committed, burst-to-800M, target $300 / 1M tokens (procurement ceiling). I'll draft two commit structures today:

A) 12-mo commit: 200M/mo @ $300 / 1M tokens, overflow billed at $375 / 1M tokens, option to scale to tiered pricing if committed volume increases.
B) Tiered commit (more aggressive): 12-mo commit with volume tiers - 0-300M: $275 / 1M, 300-600M: $225 / 1M, >600M: $175 / 1M (this hits target economics if they move more spend).

Also adding an enterprise discount if they agree to upfront annual prepay. Will attach a short estimate and the proposed SOW/PO language for Tom's review.

I'll keep it conservative on overflow pricing so it doesn't blow their monthly run-rate.

- Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Nguyen <lisa.nguyen@acmepay.com>, Tom Ramos <tom.ramos@acmepay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-20T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + budget range validation (Acme Payments)

Thanks Lisa - that's perfect, Tom - great to be looped in. Attached is a short pricing estimate (redwood-pricing-estimate-v2.pdf) with two options that map to Rishi's notes: a conservative committed baseline option and a tiered volume option that improves unit economics as usage grows.

Quick highlights in the PDF: 
- Option 1 (Conservative): 200M/mo commit @ $300 / 1M tokens; overflow at $375 / 1M. Estimated monthly range: $60k (baseline) up to higher with overflow.
- Option 2 (Tiered, more aggressive): 12-mo commit with tiers (0-300M $275 / 1M; 300-600M $225 / 1M; >600M $175 / 1M). Estimated run-rate depends on where their usage falls; at steady 400M/mo the blended rate would be ~ $237.5 / 1M (~$95k/mo).
- PO/SOW language: we included the standard SOW/PO acceptance and an option for an annual prepay discount.

Next steps / asks from Acme: 
1) Confirm which option aligns with procurement appetite (Option 1 for minimal risk vs Option 2 to hit target unit economics).
2) Confirm procurement contact email for us to send SOW/Quote (we included Tom but if there's a dedicated vendor contact send that over).
3) If you want, we can include a short 30-day pilot addendum so you can validate performance at a reduced commit before full 12-mo activation.

I'll drop the PDF in HubSpot and send a DocuSign SOW link if you indicate Option 1 or Option 2 preference.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-estimate-v2.pdf, redwood-product-sheet.pdf
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2026-03
DocuSign (SOW placeholder): https://www.docusign.com/some-sow-link-placeholder

Best - Monica
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
